title: Design a Scalable URL Shortener (TinyURL)
summary: Design a highly scalable, fault-tolerant distributed URL shortening service capable of handling hundreds of millions of daily redirections with sub-15ms latency.
description: Design a distributed URL shortening service like TinyURL or Bitly. The system allows users to submit a long URL and obtain a compact, unique alias. When users access the short link, the system redirects them to the original destination. The service must handle massive read-heavy traffic, prevent hash collision loops, ensure 99.99% redirection availability, and support optional custom aliases and click analytics.
functional_requirements: Given a long URL, generate a unique, compact 7-character short alias.
Given a short alias, redirect the client to the original long URL with sub-15ms latency.
Allow users to specify optional custom aliases with real-time uniqueness validation.
Support optional Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration timestamps for generated links.
Capture click analytics asynchronously (click count, timestamp, referrer header, user-agent, geo-location).
non_functional_requirements: High Availability: 99.99% uptime for redirection operations; read requests must succeed even during backend analytics degradation.
Ultra-low Latency: P99 redirection latency strictly under 15ms globally.
Read-Heavy Scaling: Architected for a 100:1 read-to-write traffic ratio.
Reliable Durability: Stored URL mappings must never be lost prematurely before explicit expiration.
Compact & Collision-Free: Short aliases must be 7 characters using Base62 ([a-zA-Z0-9]) providing ~3.5 trillion distinct keys without collision loops.
key_challenges: Unique alias generation at scale: Comparing Hash-and-truncate with collision retries vs Pre-generated Key Generation Service (KGS) vs Distributed Snowflake counters.
Cache stampede & eviction: Implementing Redis clusters with LRU eviction and probabilistic early expiration (XFetch) for trending/viral links.
301 Permanent Redirect vs 302 Found: Balancing client browser caching benefits with the requirement for server-side click analytics tracking.
Data partitioning & sharding: Sharding by short_key hash to eliminate hot partitions and ensure uniform cluster distribution.
Asynchronous analytics ingestion: Offloading click event logging to Kafka message queues to prevent database write bottlenecks on the redirection path.

reference_solution.architecture_pattern: Stateless microservices with distributed caching and decoupled async event stream
core_components: Global CDN & Anycast DNS for edge SSL termination and static asset caching
Stateless API Gateway / Application Service tier scaled horizontally behind L7 Load Balancer
Dedicated Key Generation Service (KGS) pre-allocating batches of unique Base62 tokens in memory
Distributed Redis Cache Cluster deployed in read-replica configuration caching hot URL mappings
Horizontally partitioned NoSQL / Key-Value Store (DynamoDB or Cassandra) partitioned by short_key
Apache Kafka message broker streaming access log events to ClickHouse for OLAP aggregation
reference_solution.short_code_strategy: Pre-generated 7-character Base62 keys from a dedicated Key Generation Service (KGS) maintaining token pools in memory, completely eliminating hash collision checks at creation time.
reference_solution.redirect_strategy: HTTP 302 Found redirect returned to force client traffic through the edge layer for real-time analytics attribution while caching mappings in Redis.
